A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Group Training work. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated supplementary material.

before.justification: v2 reports original reconstruction experiments, timing and memory measurements, sampling comparisons, and ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds rendering-efficiency diagnostics and Gaussian-projection visualizations.

M1.justification: The grouping, caching, cyclic resampling, global merging, and opacity-based sampling procedures remain unchanged. No new algorithm component, objective, or inference procedure is introduced.

E1.justification: Both evaluate novel view synthesis on Mip-NeRF360, Tanks & Temples, Deep Blending, and NeRF-Synthetic/Blender. The added diagnostics revisit the existing Train and Bicycle scenes without introducing different task requirements or environments.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator sets remain unchanged, including 3DGS, Mip-Splatting, Mini-Splatting, LightGaussian, and sampling alternatives. The new diagnostics retain the existing 3DGS-versus-Group-Training pairing; newly cited methods are not evaluated.

E3.justification: The added diagnostic evaluation measures forward-rendering FPS and hit-Gaussian counts throughout training (Appendix D, Figure 9) and visualizes projected primitives (Appendix E). Existing benchmark settings, including the 500-iteration grouping interval, 0.6 under-training ratio, and training schedule, are unchanged.

E4.justification: New appendices D–E examine the relationship between rendering speed and hit-Gaussian counts and provide a Bicycle projection case study. These supplement the retained sampling comparisons, component ablations, and primitive-count trajectory analysis.

E5.justification: Existing shaded plots in Figures 2 and 6 are retained. No repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence-interval definitions, significance tests, or other new uncertainty-reporting procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: Figure 9 adds trajectories showing higher FPS and fewer hit Gaussians with Group Training; Figure 10 adds spatial diagnostic evidence. All 16 tables remain unchanged. The PSNR/time summaries accompanying the additions reproduce results already reported in Tables 10–11.

T1.justification: The two propositions, independence assumptions, and derivations in Section 3.2 and Appendix A are retained. Mathematical expressions are unchanged apart from typesetting; removing the explanatory gloss for N does not alter Equation 8.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of Group Training's compatibility with existing 3DGS frameworks, acceleration of up to 30%, and improved rendering quality. Added diagnostics support these existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: The explanations involving fewer active primitives, opacity-driven densification and saturation, and cyclic resampling remain substantively unchanged. The new diagnostics reinforce those explanations, while the revised OPS-versus-RS discussion repeats tradeoffs already described in v2.

D1.justification: v2 promises public code upon acceptance and mentions review code in supplementary materials. v3 replaces that statement with a project-website link in the abstract. Implementation settings and hardware disclosures otherwise remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish the website's actual contents.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds citations to 3D Gaussian Splatting as Markov Chain Monte Carlo and Localized Gaussian Point Management. It also changes its characterization of earlier efficiency methods from preserving detail to sacrificing it. The additional memory-footprint reference duplicates an already cited work.

P1.justification: v3 makes local grammar and cross-reference corrections, expands affiliations, adds acknowledgements and a supplementary-material heading, and reorders appendix sections around the new diagnostics. The main narrative and document organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds a three-panel FPS/hit-count figure and a two-panel Gaussian-projection comparison. Figure 8 moves between columns, and supplementary pages reflow. Existing main figures and the structures of all 16 tables are retained.

improvement.justification: Figures 9–10 provide useful direct evidence for the existing efficiency explanation, and the project link adds concrete access information. These are limited gains on already evaluated scenes, with unchanged benchmark results and proofs. The stronger criticism of prior methods is not accompanied by expanded comparative evidence, limiting the overall benefit.
